evidence: paper: U(x,t) = \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^{3}} \widetilde{u}(x+k,t), \quad 0 \le t < 1; \qquad P_{\mathrm{per}}(x,t) = \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^{3}} \widetilde{p}(x+k,t), \quad 0 \le t < 1; \qquad F_{\mathrm{per}}(x,t) = \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^{3}} \widetilde{f}(x+k,t), \quad t \ge 0.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Lean sums f(z.1, z.2 − lattice n) over n ∈ Lattice = Fin 3 → ℤ, where the paper sums over x + k, k ∈ Z³. The reindexing k = −n is a bijection of Z³, so the two sums have the same terms; `lattice n` is the Euclidean embedding of n and `Lattice` is Z³. Lean uses an unconditional `tsum` rather than the paper's informal lattice sum; summability is supplied by summable_translate from the local finiteness of the supports, and periodize_locally_eq_sum shows it is a finite sum near every point, so the value is the paper's. The paper's range restrictions are carried by the argument of periodize rather than by the sum: U and P_per use `periodize (beforeOne u)` / `periodize (beforeOne p)`, and beforeOne zeroes t ≥ 1, matching "0 ≤ t < 1"; F_per uses `periodize f` with no restriction, matching "t ≥ 0". The Lean fields are total on all of SpaceTime (zero outside), where the paper leaves them undefined; that is a totalization convention, not a change of value on the paper's ranges.
